subject: Private Offer: procurement sign-off checklist & term options
messages:
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@amazon.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood private offer draft for Acme - AM review

Jonas/Vanessa — attaching the private offer shell from Marketplace. Acme is asking whether we can support a 24-month term with net-60 payment terms; they indicated this helps them amortize budget across two fiscal years. Two quick notes from the AM side: (1) 24-month term is allowed but requires internal approval for our co-sell co-funding (typically we look for minimum ARR/commitments); (2) for private offers that are >12 months we need the buyer to accept on behalf of their legal entity and provide a PO that references the private offer ID.

I added the Marketplace link below and flagged this to AWS Partner Sales so they can advise on co-sell enablement. If you want, we can propose an initial 12-month with an option to extend to 24 months after a renewal clause — that sometimes avoids extra AWS approvals.

Marketplace private offer link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pm-private-offers/offer/0a1b2c

Thanks,
Sasha
AWS Account Manager
Amazon Web Services
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amir Patel <amir.patel@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@amazon.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer draft for Acme - AM review

Amir — thanks for confirming your procurement preferences on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposal from our side:

- Pricing: flat unit price at $0.0009/token for inference units across the committed pool (see attached quote).
- Term: we can do a 24-month private offer, but it requires AWS co-sell signoff (Sasha has flagged). Alternate: 12-month + auto-extension clause to 24 months by mutual written consent.
- Payment: Net-60 acceptable, but for >12 months AWS requires a buyer-signed PO referencing the private offer.
- Approvals we need from Acme: legal signature on the private offer (DocuSign), procurement PO referencing the offer ID, and billing contact confirmation for invoicing.

Can you confirm whether procurement can issue a PO that references the Marketplace offer ID? If not, we can accept a Redwood invoice model but that changes the marketplace economics slightly.

Next steps: if you confirm PO capability, we'll route the 24-month private offer to Sasha for AWS approvals and circulate DocuSign to your legal. Otherwise, we can send a 12-month with extension clause today.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
(415) 555-0183
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@acme-analytics.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>, Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer draft for Acme - AM review

Jonas — procurement can issue a PO referencing the Marketplace private offer ID, but legal needs to review term length. Our procurement lead (cc'd) will need the final offer PDF and the Marketplace offer ID to embed in the PO. A couple items procurement will look for:

- Cancellation/termination rights within the term (we usually push for a 30/60-day right for material breach)
- SLA credits and data residency statements (we run EU workloads and need a statement about where inference logs are stored)
- Invoicing cadence and remittance address

If you can send the finalized offer and the DocuSign link, procurement will triage and get back within 5 business days. If legal pushes back on 24 months we may ask for a 12-month with an option to extend.

Thanks,
Amir Patel
VP Product, Acme Analytics
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer draft for Acme - AM review

Jonas — putting together the final package for procurement. Draft checklist included below (please confirm):

1) Finalized offer PDF with line items and offer ID (attached: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Quote_2026-07-22.pdf)
2) Marketplace private offer URL and internal AWS AM contact (Sasha)
3) Standard Redwood Marketplace terms + any proposed redlines (attached: Marketplace_PrivateOffer_Terms_2026-07-27.docx)
4) DocuSign envelope prepared with signature block for Acme legal + Redwood signature
5) Billing contact and remittance information for Redwood finance (billing@redwood.com)
6) Data residency note: Redwood inference will not persist inference payloads in logs for Acme's production namespace; we will provide SOC2 report on request.

Question: do we want to proactively offer a 12-month initial term with a guaranteed rate for year 2 (to reduce legal friction), or push for a full 24-month? My vote: 12+option (easier to close and keeps AWS approvals lighter).

Marissa Cole
Sr. Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@amazon.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood private offer draft for Acme - AM review

Team — quick update from AWS approval queue: we can approve co-sell credits and the 24-month duration, but only if Redwood commits to a minimum TCV threshold and we have a signed buyer PO referencing the offer ID. The approval path will add ~3 business days once documents are in Hub. If you choose 12+option we can fast-track the listing and still do a co-sell motion for year 2 renewal.

Action for Redwood: 1) upload final offer PDF to the marketplace record, 2) confirm TCV you want AWS to consider for co-sell, 3) send DocuSign to Acme legal with the offer ID included.

Sasha
AWS AM — Partner Sales
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amir Patel <amir.patel@acme-analytics.com>, procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@amazon.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: DocuSign & PO instructions for Marketplace private offer (next steps)

Amir / Procurement team — thanks for the quick replies. Attached are the final offer PDF and the Marketplace terms. We created a DocuSign envelope for Acme legal to sign that includes the private offer ID in the signature block. Link below. Once signed, please have procurement issue a PO referencing the Marketplace private offer ID and send it to billing@redwood.com.

Key items to include in PO: buyer legal name, Redwood private offer ID: 0a1b2c, invoice schedule (Net-60 per agreement), remittance instructions. If procurement prefers Redwood to invoice directly outside Marketplace we can do that, but it will change co-sell eligibility — Sasha, we assume that still works?

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/--/envelope/ABC12345
Marketplace offer: https://console.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pm-private-offers/offer/0a1b2c

We propose the following to minimize approval friction: issue a 12-month private offer with a guaranteed renewal rate for year 2, and include an express extension option exercisable by Acme at 90 days before term-end. That keeps procurement/legal happy and lets us start co-sell enablement quicker. If Acme confirms they require a firm 24-month term, we'll proceed but it will add ~3 business days for AWS co-sell signoff.

Next steps: Acme signs DocuSign (legal), procurement issues PO referencing offer ID, Sasha files for co-sell. I'll follow up once DocuSign completes.

Thanks all,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
